'''''Clematis montana''''', the '''mountain clematis''',<ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/3959/i-Clematis-montana-i/Details?returnurl=%2fplants%2fsearch-results%3fform-mode%3dtrue%26query%3dclematis%2bmontana%26aliaspath%3d%252fplants%252fsearch-results | title=''Clematis montana'' | publisher=Royal Horticultural Society | date=2017 | accessdate=2017-01-27}}</ref> also '''Himalayan clematis'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> or '''anemone clematis''', is a flowering plant in the buttercup family [[Ranunculaceae]]. A vigorous [[deciduous]] climber, in late spring it is covered with a mass of small blooms for a period of about four weeks. The odorous flowers are white or pink, four-petalled, with prominent yellow anthers. It is native to mountain areas of Asia from [[Afghanistan]] to [[Taiwan]].<ref name=FoC>{{cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200007684 |title=''Clematis montana'' |author=Wang Wencai, Bruce Bartholomew |work=Flora of China |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden, St. Louis, MO & Harvard University Herbaria, Cambridge, MA |accessdate=12 May 2013}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
''Clematis montana'' is a popular garden plant in temperate regions, with the ability to scramble up and over unsightly features such as sheds and fences. Left unchecked it can grow to {{convert|12|m|ft|abbr=on}}. ==Etymology==
''Clematis'' is the [[Greek language|Greek]] name for several climbing plants, and is a diminutive of ''klema'', meaning "vine shoot".<ref name="gledhill">Gledhill, David (2008). "The Names of Plants". Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|9780521866453}} (hardback), {{ISBN|9780521685535}} (paperback).  pp 111, 263</ref>

The Latin [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''montana'' refers to mountains or coming from mountains.<ref name="gledhill" /><ref>Archibald William Smith {{google books|ahNMkgoNJ7IC|A Gardener's Handbook of Plant Names: Their Meanings and Origins|page=239}}</ref>

==Collections==
The UK national collection of '' Clematis montana'' is held at By The Way, at [[Woodfalls]], near [[Salisbury]], Wiltshire, within the [[New Forest|New Forest National Park]]. Much of the collection has been propagated from British Clematis Society seeds.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.clematismontana.co.uk/ |title=Home |website=clematismontana.co.uk}}</ref>
